scope: H02 valid-copy selected startup-record recovery; source and controlled fixtures only
flows: Only offered after both startup reads settle and at least one record failed; editor is still gated. Physical DB initialization failure has no whole-DB restore entry.

Explicit selected SQLite file is read through no-follow file handles; exact main/WAL/SHM/journal files are copied into private temp storage and hashes/file sets are compared. SQLite operates only on private copies, no source migrations or side-file writes.

512 MiB candidate material limit, 32 MiB per selected value, integrity_check, known current tables/column order/user_version, duplicate selected rows refused; future/unknown frontend record shapes remain disabled.

Pure preview uses the same draft/setup parsers without hydration or external actions; only failed allowed records are selectable. Captured preview content remains immutable if the chosen file later changes.

Explicit confirmation asks for current-material backup location; successful full SQLite backup receipt precedes an IMMEDIATE transaction. Both raw key baselines are compared, then selected keys are atomically replaced.
The shared recovery mutex serializes command gate, preview, export, apply, receipt cache, and app_drafts_ready. Normal writing commands stay closed before editor admission.

Only unsentWork.v1 and agentSetup.v1 may be written. Other settings/credentials/account/history/permissions are not imported. A ticket caches one successful receipt by normalized key set; no second export or write on same-ticket retry.
Unknown IPC/worker result freezes recovery confirmation and offers receipt lookup; a successful receipt must match ticket and key set. No reload, queue continuation, or send is automatic.

dataProtectionEvidence: All DB and filesystem mutations used tempfile fixture directories; no ordinary app-data files or credentials were read or changed by this increment.

Shared valid-v1 fixture used in Rust two-key restore/cold-read + protected-original/other-setting preservation, and TypeScript pure preview/cold load. Only settings_get occurs during TS cold load; pending-send flags, attachments and uncertain queue index remain retained. This joins a shared data fixture across unit boundaries, not a Tauri end-to-end run.
Source fixture retained active nonempty WAL; main and exact side-file byte arrays and path sets stayed unchanged during preview.

File-change/file-set drift tests deterministically exercise the comparison boundary; source replacement after preview exercises captured-ticket application. No adversarial continuous filesystem race test is claimed.
Successful receipt retry with reversed key ordering creates no second backup; different selected set is refused.

Second-key trigger failure rolls back both originals and returns a complete protection path. Separate MetaStore tests exercise actual SQLite query_only and max_page_count-induced SQLITE_FULL, then cold-read unchanged values. Not real OS disk exhaustion.

Concurrent ready test blocks on the same recovery mutex across apply and cached receipt; pre-editor writes and pending-preview reads are refused. This is State/SQLite-level concurrency, not full IPC scheduling.
limits: Physical corrupt/unopenable current database replacement is not implemented by this increment.
No installed recovery GUI/real-user restore, screenshot validation, or real Agent call was performed. Prior SSR-browser path remains stopped by root policy.
Windows path/copy behavior is not tested; canonical path prefix differences remain an explicit platform follow-up.
No power-loss/fsync interruption or real full filesystem test. Backup helper retains earlier final-directory-fsync receipt boundary; manifest alone never certifies successful durability.

Backend enforces SQLite structure/size, JSON version, two-key scope, protection/CAS/atomicity; detailed draft/setup semantics are checked in the shared frontend pure parsers before confirmation and again before apply. Raw IPC with a syntactically v1 but semantically invalid record is outside the UI semantic proof.
No permanent restore ledger was introduced; ticket and successful receipt live only in the current process. After process restart, startup reads durable data normally.
